reason: The hook has no rule for content-printing output forms or for git show operands that are not object paths. Run: 191 tests, 175 pass, 16 fail. Unit: `git show` (no operand) is [allow, shell-identity] where [deny, shell-git-object] is expected; `git log -p` and the other patch, diff, line-log and pickaxe options are allowed where shell-git-output is expected; `git status -v` is allowed; `git log -p --oneline` and `git log --oneline -p` are allowed. semanticAssessment: Each failure is on the planned assertion for the intended reason: the target tests executed on a built sentinel-bearing repository (the admitted-forms and Task 1 leak tests ran real git and the hook on the same repository and passed), and the actual value is the hook allowing a form the plan refuses (output option or non-object git show operand) where the rule is shell-git-object or shell-git-output. In the integration leak tests the hook assertion is the first to fail, so the git-prints-the-sentinel half of those tests is exercised only once the rule exists; it is observed in the GREEN run. No failure is a syntax, import or fixture fault. The allowed-list and earlier-rule tests pass at base by design: they pin existing behaviour that the narrowing must keep.
summary: Run of the two files: 191 tests, 175 pass, 16 fail (4 unit, 12 integration). The hook allows `git log -p`, `git status -v`, `git show`, `git show HEAD` and the blob forms that real git prints the secret for.
